verdict.rationale: Proa's own materials say it can flush server-rendered HTML in document order, or let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order so slow data does not block the page. Its islands architecture ships server-rendered HTML with only small per-island JS modules, so content can render before client code loads. Missing for 10: in-depth docs on the streaming API and its configuration, and independent or hands-on corroboration of perceived-load gains.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream server-rendered content so pages get faster perceived loads before all client code arrives

citations.quote: Flush HTML in document order when sequence matters, or let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order when slow data should not block the page.
Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
